data.name: FileMenu
data.comment: The command bar button that opens the menu with Open, Save and Save as, as in Paint or Notepad; also its screen reader name. Use the word Windows apps use for their File menu. Keep it to about 12 characters.

data.name: Open
data.comment: The File menu item that opens a project file (a dialog follows, hence the ellipsis). Use Windows' own word for Open.

data.name: Save
data.comment: The File menu item that saves the project to its file (the first time, a Save dialog opens). Use Windows' own word for Save.

data.name: SaveAs
data.comment: The File menu item that saves the project to a new file through a Save dialog. Use Windows' own words for Save as.

data.name: FileTypeName
data.comment: The name of the .10lapse file type in the Open and Save dialogs. 10Lapse is the app's name and never changes.

data.name: OpenNotAProjectFormat
data.value: “{0}” isn't a 10Lapse project, or it's damaged, so it couldn't be opened.
data.comment: A Critical InfoBar. {0} the file's name with its extension ("Harbor.10lapse").

data.name: OpenUnreadableFormat
data.value: “{0}” couldn't be opened. Check that it's still there and that you can read it, then try again.
data.comment: A Critical InfoBar when the file cannot be read (gone, locked, no access). {0} the file's name with its extension.

data.name: OpenNewerVersionFormat
data.value: “{0}” was saved by a newer version of 10Lapse. Settings this version doesn't know were left out.
data.comment: A Caution InfoBar after opening a project file from a newer 10Lapse; the project opened. {0} the file's name with its extension.

data.name: OpenSomeSettingsFormat
data.value: Some settings in “{0}” couldn't be read and were set back to their defaults.
data.comment: A Caution InfoBar after opening a project file with a damaged setting; the project opened. {0} the file's name with its extension.

data.name: MissingPhotos_one
data.value: {0} photo of this project wasn't found and was left out. Put it back where it was, then open the project again.
data.comment: A Caution InfoBar after opening a project, with a list of the photos behind "View list". {0} the count. Removing never deletes: the photo was moved or deleted outside 10Lapse.

data.name: MissingPhotos_other
data.value: {0} photos of this project weren't found and were left out. Put them back where they were, then open the project again.
data.comment: As MissingPhotos_one, for other counts. {0} the count, already written in the user's format ("1,240").

data.name: SaveFailedFormat
data.value: “{0}” couldn't be saved. Check that its folder is still there and that you can write to it, then try again.
data.comment: A Critical InfoBar when writing the project file fails; the file on disk is unchanged. {0} the file's name with its extension.

data.name: UnsavedTitleFormat
data.comment: The title of the question before unsaved changes would be lost (opening another project, closing the window). {0} the project's name.

data.name: UnsavedMessage
data.value: If you don't save, your changes to this project will be lost.
data.comment: The question's text.

data.name: UnsavedSave
data.comment: The question's default button: saves, then goes on. Keep it to about 16 characters.

data.name: UnsavedDontSave
data.comment: The question's button that goes on without saving. Use the words Windows apps use. Keep it to about 16 characters.

data.name: RecoveryOfferFormat
data.value: 10Lapse closed before your changes to “{0}” were saved. Restore them to carry on where you left off.
data.comment: An InfoBar at launch after 10Lapse ended without closing (a crash, a power cut) with unsaved changes. {0} the project's name ("Harbor sunset"). 10Lapse never changes.

data.name: RecoveryRestore
data.comment: The recovery InfoBar's button: opens the unsaved project as it was. Not the word for Undo. Keep it to about 16 characters.

data.name: RecentHeading
data.comment: The heading over the list of recently opened or saved projects on the first-launch screen.

data.name: RecentClear
data.comment: A text button beside the heading that empties the recent list (the files stay). Keep it to about 16 characters.

data.name: RecentClearName
data.value: Clear the list of recent projects
data.comment: The screen reader name of the Clear list button.

data.name: RecentNotFound
data.comment: Beside a recent project whose file was moved or deleted. Keep it to about 14 characters.

data.name: RecentItemNameFormat
data.comment: A recent project's screen reader name. {0} the project's name ("Harbor sunset"), {1} its folder ("D:\Trips").

data.name: RecentItemMissingNameFormat
data.comment: A missing recent project's screen reader name. {0} the project's name, {1} the RecentNotFound note.

data.name: RecentGoneFormat
data.value: “{0}” isn't where it was saved any more, so it was taken off the list.
data.comment: A Caution InfoBar after clicking a recent project whose file is gone. {0} the project's name.
